Obtained result: a certified family of recurrent reaction-record inferences

I developed two complementary constructions beyond the single-opening interface.

The stronger repeated-inference operation now handles a hidden recurrent controller, genuinely coupled reaction hazards, overlapping reaction interfaces, and repeated conditioning while preserving a fixed number of retained mixture components. Its certificate can cover an entire bounded observation workload before the particular record is known.

A second construction removes the unchanged-silent-generator restriction: when the local killed generators commute, recurrent controller dynamics can be integrated through occupation moments, with a proved bound on the number of positive product operators required.

Both have new executable code and actual retained rational operators. The repeated-inference construction also reused the existing correlated entrance and retained its resulting posterior. The mathematical extensions and executed specializations are distinguished below.

The candidate contribution is now quite specific:

Obtain, from checked compact rules, an executable reaction-query interface together with a representation bound and a conditional-law error bound for a declared family of future observations.

The comparison with established methods concerns that complete obtaining-and-execution contract. Occupation formulas, trajectory conditioning, positive operators, averaging and projective error propagation each have substantial antecedents.

Consider a symmetric hidden controller Ct∈{−1,+1}C_t\in\{-1,+1\}Ct​∈{−1,+1}, switching at rate ν\nuν. The local physical components have finite silent generators QiQ_iQi​, independent of the controller within this construction. Their initial distribution may be arbitrarily correlated.

Let V(c,x)V(c,x)V(c,x) be the total hazard of all recorded reactions. The checked source establishes

V(c,x)=Vˉ(x)+c h(x),∣h(x)∣≤A,V(c,x)=\bar V(x)+c\,h(x), \qquad |h(x)|\le A,V(c,x)=Vˉ(x)+ch(x),∣h(x)∣≤A,

with

Vˉ(x)=d0+∑idi(xi),d0,di≥0.\bar V(x)=d_0+\sum_i d_i(x_i), \qquad d_0,d_i\ge 0.Vˉ(x)=d0​+i∑​di​(xi​),d0​,di​≥0.

The actual hazards V(+1,⋅)V(+1,\cdot)V(+1,⋅) and V(−1,⋅)V(-1,\cdot)V(−1,⋅) may couple overlapping components throughout a connected graph. Only their mean is additive.

For an observed mark jjj, retain its exact nonnegative guard/reset operator JjJ_jJj​. Define the reference event-density operator

Kˉj(t)=e−d0t[Pν(t)⊗⨂ie(Qi−Di)t]Jj,Di=diag⁡(di).\bar K_j(t)= e^{-d_0t} \left[ P_\nu(t)\otimes \bigotimes_i e^{(Q_i-D_i)t} \right]J_j, \qquad D_i=\operatorname{diag}(d_i).Kˉj​(t)=e−d0​t[Pν​(t)⊗i⨂​e(Qi​−Di​)t]Jj​,Di​=diag(di​).

The quantifiers matter: this holds for every joint input and output coordinate, before choosing an entrance distribution. It consequently applies to correlated entrances, deterministic entrances and entrances correlated with spectator historical variables.

Why the comparison works

Fix any silent leaf trajectory. Its interaction with the controller becomes a bounded time-dependent potential h(s)h(s)h(s), with ∣h(s)∣≤A|h(s)|\le A∣h(s)∣≤A.

For the lower bound, the exact controller-bridge mean is

Its integrated absolute value is at most tanh⁡(νt)/ν\tanh(\nu t)/\nutanh(νt)/ν. Jensen’s inequality therefore gives the lower multiplier.

For the upper bound, transform the controller into its mass/imbalance basis. The free generator becomes diag⁡(0,−2ν)\operatorname{diag}(0,-2\nu)diag(0,−2ν). Absolute values of the time-ordered potential terms are bounded by the positive comparison matrix

M=(0AA−2ν).M= \begin{pmatrix} 0&A\\ A&-2\nu \end{pmatrix}.M=(0A​A−2ν​).

This bridge/Feynman–Kac reasoning has close antecedents. Leschke and colleagues explicitly treat two-state endpoint transforms and time-dependent fields; Paulin’s concentration results for inhomogeneous chains also imply the qualitative fast-switching scale. The new claim is the source acquisition and executable representation obtained from those ingredients, rather than a new general averaging principle. arxiv.org+1

Obtaining the conditions from rules

The new compiler checks the controller’s autonomy and symmetry, obtains the local silent generators, and verifies their equality across controller phases.

It converts each Boolean equality guard into an exact rational multilinear polynomial. Summing all marked hazards and averaging the two phases exposes whether the coefficients of degree greater than one cancel. The contrast bound AAA is obtained by enumerating individual small guard scopes and summing valid local bounds. Overlapping scopes can make that bound conservative; they do not invalidate it.

The implemented source language is finite guarded Boolean rules, with a bounded guard-scope budget. It is not a general Kappa or BioNetGen graph-rewriting compiler.

2. The stronger operation: repeated filtering without mixture growth

An operator certificate alone does not control the cost of repeated inference. The additional result is a checked closure condition for the retained probability representation.

Suppose the current retained law is

The mixture label retains correlations between components and with the controller. Nothing requires the overall law to factor.

Assume an identified mark jjj:

  • reads a set SjS_jSj​ of local components;
  • resets every component on which its hazard or hidden branch choice depends;
  • gives those components the same public product reset state in every unobserved branch.

The controller may remain unchanged. More generally, its reset may depend on the active pre-event variables: that dependence can be integrated into its small output row.

For one incoming mixture component, let the propagated raw rows be

gr(d)=∑cpr(c)∑xSjhj(c,xSj,d)∏i∈Sjvri(xi).g_r(d)= \sum_c p_r(c) \sum_{x_{S_j}} h_j(c,x_{S_j},d) \prod_{i\in S_j}v_{ri}(x_i).gr​(d)=c∑​pr​(c)xSj​​∑​hj​(c,xSj​​,d)i∈Sj​∏​vri​(xi​).

The inactive components factor out. The active components are pinned to their common reset states. Thus one input product component produces one output product component, after its full event-density mass is retained.

Induction gives:

Every admitted sequence of identified events preserves at most RRR mixture components, even when active scopes overlap and the recurrent controller remains unobserved.

This is exact closure of the retained approximation. The true coupled posterior is enclosed by the certificate; it is not asserted to have the same finite product-mixture rank.

For binary components, an update costs

O ⁣(R(n+Bjs))O\!\left(R(n+B_js)\right)O(R(n+Bj​s))

scalar operations when the selected mark has BjB_jBj​ guard branches of scope at most sss. Storage is O(Rn)O(Rn)O(Rn) scalar entries plus the rule interface. Precision and rational bit lengths remain additional costs. The calculation does not enumerate controller switch trajectories.

What must be retained during normalization

Each local row has a survival mass. The controller row also has a mass after numerical enclosure and event selection. All those masses contribute to the component’s event density and hence to its updated mixture weight.

The implementation retains them and normalizes by the complete mixture event density. It does not separately normalize event-kernel rows before mixing.

This is also why an observed event can strongly change the controller posterior even when the controller switches rapidly: the exact terminal guard selects controller phases differently.

Where closure fails

The condition applies to the state actually retained.

If a physical leaf is reset but its historical count label remains, that label can still carry dependence on the controller and other leaves. The existing count tensor train therefore does not automatically inherit this fixed-width result.

Likewise, a coarse mark that could reset different locations or different output states generally creates extra mixture components. Coarsening over guard branches is inexpensive here because those branches share the same complete leaf reset.

These are explicit representation boundaries, separate from the validity of the relative certificate.

The new callable workload_certificate(...) checks every admitted mark’s reset structure and certifies a family of records.

A simpler sufficient bound is

log⁡Ranalytic≤2MA+A2T/2ν.\boxed{ \log R_{\mathrm{analytic}} \le \frac{2MA+A^2T/2}{\nu}. }logRanalytic​≤ν2MA+A2T/2​.​

Let R0R_0R0​ be the inherited projective spread of the entrance and Γnum\Gamma_{\rm num}Γnum​ the total numerical log-spread actually allowed or incurred. Then the whole conditional-state error is bounded by

TV⁡≤tanh⁡ ⁣[log⁡R0+Γnum+log⁡Ranalytic4].\operatorname{TV} \le \tanh\!\left[ \frac{ \log R_0+\Gamma_{\rm num} +\log R_{\mathrm{analytic}} }{4} \right].TV≤tanh[4logR0​+Γnum​+logRanalytic​​].

This is the established projective-to-TV mechanism applied to the newly obtained workload. Its strength is that the bound does not divide by the likelihood of the selected record. arxiv.org

For a requested tolerance ϵ\epsilonϵ, a sufficient eligibility test is

Δ=4atanh⁡(ϵ)−log⁡R0−Γnum>0,\Delta= 4\operatorname{atanh}(\epsilon) -\log R_0-\Gamma_{\rm num}>0,Δ=4atanh(ϵ)−logR0​−Γnum​>0,ν≥2MA+A2T/2Δ.\boxed{ \nu\ge \frac{2MA+A^2T/2}{\Delta}. }ν≥Δ2MA+A2T/2​.​

The controller rate is a supplied scientific parameter. This test decides whether the declared source and workload meet the error target; it does not change that parameter.

A terminal interval with no event is another propagation operation and must be included in the accounting. The initial entrance uncertainty is paid once. Every newly approximated propagation and numerical application pays its own spread.

Consequently, fixed representation width does not imply fixed error over an unlimited record.

A distinction about the retained operator family

Keeping exact marked jumps while replacing their total killing by its mean does not automatically produce a conservative reduced marked CTMC. The retained objects are positive, certified record-likelihood operators.

Their normalizers are event-time densities. A complete finite-horizon positive path measure can be defined and globally normalized, but that does not establish local generator conservation or a cheap simulator for that globally normalized measure.

The code and proofs preserve this distinction.

4. Exact additive cancellation can be relaxed

I also proved an extension that removes exact cancellation as a binary mathematical admission condition.

Suppose

Vˉ(x)=v0+∑idˉi(xi)+r(x),r−≤r(x)≤r+,\bar V(x) = v_0+\sum_i \bar d_i(x_i)+r(x), \qquad r_-\le r(x)\le r_+,Vˉ(x)=v0​+i∑​dˉi​(xi​)+r(x),r−​≤r(x)≤r+​,

  • rapid controller switching controls the centered phase contrast;
  • the remaining nonadditive mean has its own explicit error cost;
  • making the controller faster cannot remove that residual cost.

The fast-controller route still requires unchanged silent generators. The second construction addresses that restriction under a different source condition.

What must be retained during normalization

Each local row has a survival mass. The controller row also has a mass after numerical enclosure and event selection. All those masses contribute to the component’s event density and hence to its updated mixture weight.

The implementation retains them and normalizes by the complete mixture event density. It does not separately normalize event-kernel rows before mixing.

This is also why an observed event can strongly change the controller posterior even when the controller switches rapidly: the exact terminal guard selects controller phases differently.

Where closure fails

The condition applies to the state actually retained.

If a physical leaf is reset but its historical count label remains, that label can still carry dependence on the controller and other leaves. The existing count tensor train therefore does not automatically inherit this fixed-width result.

Likewise, a coarse mark that could reset different locations or different output states generally creates extra mixture components. Coarsening over guard branches is inexpensive here because those branches share the same complete leaf reset.

These are explicit representation boundaries, separate from the validity of the relative certificate.

8. What remains outside the completed capability

The two main routes have different conditions. They do not jointly establish tractability for arbitrary recurrent controllers, arbitrary changed silent generators and arbitrary coupled hazards.

The substantive remaining boundaries are:

General controller feedback. The controller is autonomous between recorded events.
General changed silent dynamics. Occupation compression requires local killed-generator commutation. The separate noncommuting splitting proof gives a relative-certified circuit under additional support conditions, but generic contraction may still be exponential.
Arbitrary coarse observations. Unknown event locations, differing hidden reset outputs and retained historical count allocations can increase representation size.
